children: Shares of IM Cannabis rose after the company said it had regained compliance with Nasdaq's minimum bid price requirement.
The stock was up 8.6% to $3.16 in after-hours trading on Wednesday. The shares closed down 30% at $2.91, and have fallen 93% this year.

The medical cannabis company said it received notice from Nasdaq that it had regained compliance with the rule after the closing price of its shares was $1.00 or greater for 18 consecutive business days between Aug. 27 and Sept. 22.
